title: The Lord looketh on the heart (1 Samuel 16:7)
hook: the youngest shepherd is chosen, not the tall brothers

segments.voice: Yesterday, shema, to hear, the verb Samuel used: to obey is better than sacrifice. Your line was do the plain thing. Today, Samuel goes looking for the next king.

A horn of oil, and a dangerous errand. Samuel is sent to Bethlehem, to the house of Jesse, because God has chosen a king from among his sons. Samuel is afraid: if Saul hears, he'll kill me. So he goes with a heifer to offer a sacrifice, and invites Jesse and his sons. The first son walks in, Eliab, the eldest, and Samuel thinks: surely this is the one. He looks like a king. Last time, Israel got a king who stood head and shoulders above everyone. This must be him.
screen: `A HORN OF OIL, TO BETHLEHEM.` → `ELIAB WALKS IN.` → `SURELY THIS IS THE ONE.`

segments.voice: And God says no. Look not on his countenance, or on the height of his stature, because I have rejected him. Then the line the chapter turns on: "for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart." Even a prophet, even Samuel, judged by height. Jesse brings the next son, Abinadab. Not this one. Then Shammah. Not this one. Jesse makes seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and to each the answer is the same: the LORD has not chosen these. So Samuel asks, almost funnily: are these all your children? Well, says Jesse, there's still the youngest. He's out keeping the sheep. Nobody thought to call him in. Send and fetch him, Samuel says; we won't sit down until he comes. So everyone waits, standing, for a boy to come in from the field. And when David arrives, the text describes him: ruddy, with beautiful eyes, and good to look at. The same chapter that says don't look at appearances tells us he was handsome. Some readers find a little joke in that: the point was never that looks are bad, only that they aren't what God goes by. Arise, anoint him, God says, for this is he. Samuel anoints him in the middle of his brothers, and the spirit of the LORD comes on David from that day forward. The brothers in the room are passed over; the one left in the field is chosen.
screen: `EVEN SAMUEL JUDGED BY HEIGHT.` · `SEVEN SONS, AND NOT THESE.` · `THE YOUNGEST, OUT WITH THE SHEEP.` · `HANDSOME TOO, AND THAT'S NOT WHY.` · then, large: `THE LORD LOOKETH ON THE HEART.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you've sized up by how they look, sound or dress, or what they do for work: a coworker, a neighbor, maybe you, in the mirror. Set the outside aside and ask: what do I actually know about their heart, and what have they carried? If you don't know, just notice that; if you pray, hold Samuel's lesson: the LORD looketh on the heart.
David. The youngest son left out in the field, ruddy and good to look at, chosen because God looks on the heart, not the height.
Your line: the heart, not the height. Even Samuel had to learn it. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Jews read David's anointing in Bethlehem as part of the Former Prophets, and the line that God looks on the heart is studied as a teaching about not judging by appearances.

chat.says: Why did God pick David, the youngest, over his older brothers who looked like kings?
options: God looks on the heart, not appearance; even Samuel judged by height and was corrected.
David was the tallest and strongest son, so he looked the most like a king.
The older brothers turned the crown down, so the youngest was the only one left.
chat.meaning: Samuel was sure Eliab was the one. God said: man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

Bethlehem.meaning: Jesse's town, where Samuel came with a horn of oil

Jesse.meaning: David's father, whose sons passed before Samuel

Eliab.meaning: Jesse's eldest son, who looked like a king

Abinadab.meaning: Jesse's second son to pass before Samuel

sources.quoted: for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart.

notes: Verify JPS 1917 wording of the 16:7 fragment (certain in the KJV).
'Seven of his sons' is in 16:10. Eliab, Abinadab and Shammah are named in 16:6–9.
'Last time Israel got a king who stood a head above everyone' recalls 10:23 (day 732).
'Some readers find that a little joke in the text' is attributed, not asserted.
Original: לֵבָב is the form in 16:7 ('yir'eh lalevav'); confirm (vs. לֵב) and the pronunciation.
The word segment says God 'sees the heart'; the text says 'looketh on'. Acceptable paraphrase; editor check.

Editor: 'the tallest son' changed to 'the eldest son' and 'the tall brothers in their best clothes' to 'the brothers in the room' (only Eliab's height is implied, and no clothes are mentioned); 1 Samuel 17:13 added to sources because 16:1–13 never calls Eliab the eldest; 'a head above' aligned with 10:23's 'from his shoulders and upward'.
